subject: Access trail residency & export process — scoping questions
message_1_subject: Questions on access trails: residency, retention, and full exports
message_1_body:
Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. A few quick scoping questions from our side as we prepare an eDiscovery request: 

1) What are Redwood's default retention windows for access trails vs. audit logs on the hosted API? Do Dedicated/Private deployments let customers set retention independently?
2) For exports: can you provide whole-log exports (raw events with full metadata) or only aggregated/audit summaries? Preferred formats (Parquet/CSV/NDJSON)?
3) Residency: if we request an export, does Redwood allow us to specify the export destination region (US vs EU) and deliver directly to our customer-controlled S3 bucket?
4) Chain-of-custody: do exported bundles include a signed manifest and checksums? Is there any time-bounded access URL or transfer log we can use for forensic evidence?
5) PII handling: can PII fields be redacted or hashed on export (field-level hashing) and do you include the hashing salt/strategy in the manifest?

We're also interested in SLA for a bulk export (e.g., 30-day window, ~200M events). Please see attached scoping-questionnaire.pdf for context.

Appreciate a short Q&A or a checklist we can pass to legal/forensics.

Thanks,
Sarah Bennett
Security Ops
Acme Corp
message_2_subject: Re: Questions on access trails: residency, retention, and full exports
message_2_body:
Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; happy to follow up with a short call if you'd like concrete timelines for your 200M-event request.

1) Retention windows
- Hosted (default): access logs = 90 days; audit logs (control-plane/audit events) = 365 days for enterprise customers on the Audit Add-on.
- Dedicated/Private: retention is customer-configurable; we provide a retention policy control and local deletion tooling.

2) Export granularity & formats
- We can export raw event streams (full metadata) or summarized audit exports. Supported formats: gzipped Parquet (preferred for columnar forensic analysis), CSV, NDJSON. Exports include a schema/manifest CSV that lists fields and types.

3) Residency and destination controls
- For Hosted: exports can be delivered to a customer S3 bucket in a specified region (we require an admin-supplied write role or presigned upload). For EU-residency customers we will route export job execution to the EU bucket and keep temporary staging in EU.
- Dedicated/Private: export operations run inside customer environment; data never leaves the environment unless you configure an outbound transfer.

4) Chain-of-custody and integrity
- Exports include a signed manifest (PKI signature from Redwood), per-file checksums (SHA256), and an audit log of export-job events. We also provide an export job ID you can cite in legal requests.

5) PII handling
- We support field-level redaction and deterministic hashing for export. Hashing salt is customer-controlled for Private; for Hosted we can provide a redaction-only export or reversible pseudonymization under a mutual agreement (we avoid shipping salts unless contractually required). The manifest will indicate which fields were redacted/hashed.

Next steps: I attached our export_schema_v1.csv to show field names. For your 30-day / 200M event export we typically scope it as a background bulk job — expected turnaround for Hosted is 48–96 hours after scoping & permissions are in place (subject to queue and region). For very large windows we recommend a staged export (chunked by day) which we can automate.

If acceptable, I can draft a short export checklist for legal/forensics and schedule a test export next week.

Best,
Irene Choi
Product Security
Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Fwd: Access trail residency & export process — scoping questions
message_3_body:
Irene / team — quick internal notes before we lock the reply: 

- Confirm Hosted defaults (90/365) in the public KB and include link.
- For EU customers explicitly state "exports executed in-region and delivered to EU buckets only" — avoids cross-border questions.
- Add a sentence about retention deletion proofs (we can provide deletion event logs for Private/Dedicated via the control plane).

Proposed one-line for EU customers: "For customers requiring EU residency, export jobs and temporary staging will be executed in our EU region and we will deliver only to a customer-controlled EU destination; no export artifacts are staged in non-EU regions."

If you want I can add the KB link and ship that as a follow-up.

-Hannah
message_4_subject: Re: Access trail residency & export process — scoping questions
message_4_body:
Thanks, Irene — that helps a lot. We'd like to proceed with a test export for a 7-day window first to verify schema and hashing behavior. Can Redwood: 

- Provide a sample export manifest for a 7-day test (Parquet + manifest + SHA256 checksums)
- Deliver the test to our S3 (we will provide write role)
- Provide the export job ID and signed manifest (chain-of-custody PDF) when done

Attached: export_sample_manifest.csv and a short eDiscovery scope doc. Can you confirm ETA for the test export and any cost/credits we should expect?

Thanks — Sarah
